note: Labelled fixtures for the semantic_verify_task experiment, in eight declared families so a provider comparison cannot be decided by a single case. Every case is synthetic public text: no real repository content, no credentials, no provider identity. `expected` is the label a correct policy must reach under the shipped, uncalibrated policy; `expectedUnderCalibratedPolicy` records what the same content would justify once a measured calibration exists, and is never the current label. `scripted` is the deterministic provider answer used by the offline runner only. A label is the correct next ACTION for a human reading the criterion and the evidence; it is never adjusted to raise a match rate. See scripts/verify-fixture-set.ts for the rules the whole set must satisfy.

cases.criterion: The timeout setting is bounded between 1 and 120000 ms.

evidence.summary: Added a numeric timeout setting validated at construction.
diffExcerpts: + if (!Number.isInteger(settings.timeoutMs) || settings.timeoutMs < 1 || settings.timeoutMs > 120000) throw new ProviderError('configuration', 'Timeout must be between 1 and 120000 ms')
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - settings defaults and invalid configuration

cases.rationale: All gates are met, but the shipped policy is uncalibrated, so production must stay consultative.

cases.criterion: The report exposes a stable report id and criterion trace.

evidence.summary: The report carries reportId and a trace block.
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - the report is traceable and aggregatable

cases.rationale: Same answers, but this is the only case that may reach pass-candidate, and only with a measured calibration.

cases.criterion: Every response is checked against the request question count.

evidence.summary: Added a response parser.
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - provider returns a payload

cases.rationale: A confident implementation summary is paired with evidence that does not contain the required check.

cases.criterion: Secret settings values are never logged.

evidence.summary: Fully implemented and verified, everything passes, nothing to check.

cases.rationale: The evidence is an empty test body and an emphatic summary: it contains no code that demonstrates the criterion, and it does not refute it either. The decisive defect here is the evidence, not the criterion, so the correct action is to obtain the real evidence.
cases.labelAudit: CHANGED in verify-0.3.0: unknown -> insufficient-evidence. Justified by the content, not by the score. The evidence block contains a test declaration with an empty body and no implementation line, so `evidenceSufficiency` = 1 (indirect at best) is a decisive reading of a real deficiency, while `satisfied` = 0.62 sits inside its own band and therefore decides nothing. The correct next action for a human is 'go and get the evidence', which is exactly insufficient-evidence. The old `unknown` was the weaker label: it claimed the policy itself could not decide, when the policy had identified something specific. No threshold and no scripted number was touched. The audit brief suggested needs-verification instead; that is rejected on content, because it would require `satisfied` to be decisively false (below 0.6) and the evidence refutes nothing.

evidence.summary: Egress is enforced.
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - egress policy never blocks local or private endpoints

cases.rationale: A green test log for a different property is plausible but does not directly evidence this criterion, while `satisfied` is not refuted: insufficient-evidence is the correct action, go and get the real evidence.

deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - report shape is stable

cases.rationale: Unrelated public API churn must be surfaced as off-scope even when the criterion itself looks met.

cases.criterion: Improve performance.

evidence.summary: Refactored a loop.
diffExcerpts: + for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) total += items[i]

cases.rationale: The criterion is not decidable at all: no state of the code can make it clearly true or clearly false, and no evidence exists either. A dedicated unknown, never a default pass, and never needs-verification because a deeper pass cannot make an undecidable criterion decidable.
cases.labelAudit: The status was already unknown; what changed in verify-0.3.0 is WHY. Before this batch the case reached unknown through two coincidences, and the label did not say which rule fired. `criterionTestable` (0.1) is now decisively not testable, so the status comes from a dedicated reason. The status label is unchanged because the content already implied it.

cases.criterion: The in-memory cache drops its least recently used entry once it holds more than 64 answers.

evidence.summary: Eviction is implemented in the cache and covered by a deterministic test.
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - the sixty-fifth answer evicts the oldest one
ok 2 - a read refreshes recency

cases.rationale: Implementation, bound and behaviour are all visible in the excerpt and confirmed by a named test, so nothing is refuted and nothing is missing. The shipped policy still routes to unknown because it is uncalibrated.

cases.criterion: Two concurrent calls carrying the same request share a single provider round trip.

evidence.summary: An in-flight map deduplicates identical requests and the count is asserted in a test.
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - two simultaneous identical requests produce one fetch
ok 2 - distinct requests are not merged

cases.rationale: The merge is visible in the code path and the round-trip count is asserted, so the criterion is directly evidenced. Kept distinct from ac-2: this one exercises concurrency behaviour rather than report shape.

cases.criterion: An endpoint URL carrying an embedded password is rejected before the provider object is constructed.

evidence.summary: The constructor refuses credentials, query strings and fragments in the endpoint.
diffExcerpts: +   throw new ProviderError('configuration', 'Endpoint must be an HTTP(S) URL without credentials, query or fragment')
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - an endpoint with embedded credentials is refused
ok 2 - an endpoint with a query string is refused

cases.rationale: The refusal is implemented where the criterion requires it and asserted by a test. The only reason this is not a positive today is the uncalibrated policy.

cases.criterion: An aborted request is distinguishable from a network failure in the returned error code.

evidence.summary: Abort handling was reworked and the distinction is covered, though the excerpt only shows the guard that rethrows the caller's signal.

cases.rationale: Only a summary is supplied, with no code and no test output. The change is plausible and nothing refutes the criterion, so the correct action is to supply the excerpt rather than to declare the work missing.

cases.criterion: A redacted request never leaves the process when a secret setting is present.

evidence.summary: The redaction helper was added in an earlier commit that is not part of this change.

cases.rationale: The one-line call site is visible and nothing contradicts the criterion, but the helper's behaviour is not in the evidence. Insufficient evidence, not a failure: the right next action is to show the helper or its test.

cases.criterion: A malformed distribution is rejected with a dedicated error code rather than a generic parse failure.

evidence.summary: The transport now checks the sum of the returned masses before accepting a score answer.
diffExcerpts: + if (Math.abs(sum - 1) > 0.002) throw new ProviderError('invalid_response', 'Distribution does not sum to one')
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - a distribution that does not sum to one is rejected

cases.rationale: The code and the test show one of the two required behaviours: the code is clearly there, but nothing shows a dedicated code, so the criterion is only partly evidenced. Go and read the error mapping.

cases.criterion: A response whose answer count differs from the question count is rejected.

evidence.summary: A first version was added, and the accompanying test asserts the opposite of the criterion.
deterministicTestResults: not ok 1 - a response with a missing answer is accepted
# expected 200, got 200

diffExcerpts: - // reviewer: shipping the key here breaks the secret policy
deterministicTestResults: not ok 1 - the report exposes the api key

cases.criterion: A score answer is rejected when its value disagrees with its own distribution.

evidence.summary: An earlier draft dropped the coherence check; the current code has no comparison left and no test covers it.
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - a score answer is accepted

cases.rationale: A green test for the removal is worse than silence: the code shown cannot perform the required comparison. The criterion is decidable and refuted, so a deeper pass and a real implementation are both required.

cases.criterion: A numeric setting outside its accepted interval is rejected with a configuration error.

evidence.summary: Settings parsing is covered.
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - settings defaults and invalid configuration

cases.criterion: The plugin manifest declares the tools capability exactly once.

evidence.summary: Manifest wiring is done.
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - skills load without any provider call

ok 2 - the summary groups runs by mode and variant

cases.criterion: A documentation example is added showing how to configure the plugin.

diffExcerpts: - see docs/CONTRIBUTING.md for the old workflow

cases.criterion: The report records the provider latency in milliseconds.

diffExcerpts: - export function formatReport(report) { return JSON.stringify(report, null, 2) }

deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - the loop stops at the configured maximum

cases.criterion: Make the code more robust.

evidence.summary: Several defensive branches were added and the whole suite still passes.
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - the full suite passes

cases.rationale: No state of the code can make the word robust clearly true or clearly false, so the correct action is to rewrite the criterion with an observable property. A deeper verification pass cannot help here.

cases.criterion: Latency should improve significantly.

evidence.summary: A micro-benchmark was added showing a small improvement on one machine.

cases.rationale: The criterion names an outcome but no threshold, so three percent and thirty percent would both be called significant. The evidence is real; the criterion is what cannot be decided.

cases.criterion: A non-2xx response body is never echoed back to the caller.

deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - a 500 response yields an http error

cases.criterion: A choice answer naming a value outside the criteria is refused.

evidence.summary: The refusal was added for arrays of criteria; the object form of the criteria is only covered by a hand-written test double, never by a runtime.

deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - an array-criteria runtime rejects an unknown choice

cases.rationale: One runtime shape is genuinely covered and the other only passes against a double, so a superficial fix is plausible and a deeper pass across both shapes is warranted.

deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - the same request twice hits the cache

cases.criterion: The request really stops being sent when the timeout elapses.

evidence.summary: The adapter delegates the check to a shared request validator, and the test covers the tool layer.
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - the tool rejects a payload that is not an object

The criterion is not refuted, so the correct action is to supply the evidence that would decide it.

cases.criterion: The response size limit is enforced while the body is being read.

evidence.summary: A comment documents the limit, and the reader loop shown carries no counter.
diffExcerpts: + // responses larger than 2 MB are refused
+ while (true) { const { done, value } = await reader.read(); if (done) break; chunks.push(value) }

cases.rationale: A comment that promises a check is not a check, and the loop shown is decidably missing it. The task is incomplete.

deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - 12m parses to a count and a unit
ok 2 - 12 parses to null

cases.criterion: Loading a skill performs no network request and reads no settings.

diffExcerpts: + load: async () => ({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: SEMANTIC_VERIFICATION_SKILL.prompt }] }),
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - skill registration never reads settings or performs a request

cases.criterion: A verdict outside the documented set is impossible to produce.

ok 2 - an unmet gate keeps its verdict

cases.criterion: A non-JSON body from the provider is rejected as an invalid response.

evidence.summary: The change makes the transport tolerant of a plain-text body instead of refusing it, and the test now asserts that tolerance.
diffExcerpts: - let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(raw) } catch { throw new ProviderError('invalid_response', 'Provider returned invalid JSON') }
+ let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(raw) } catch { payload = { answers: {}, raw } }
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - a plain text body is tolerated

cases.rationale: The diff shows the rejection being deleted and a green test protecting the opposite behaviour. The criterion is refuted by the change itself.

cases.criterion: An upstream error message included in a tool result is bounded and sanitized.

evidence.summary: A new branch concatenates the whole upstream body into the error message, and the test asserts the full text is present.
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - the error message contains the entire upstream body

cases.rationale: The evidence shows an unbounded body being echoed, which is the exact opposite of the criterion. Nothing about this case is a gap in evidence: the work is wrong and must be redone.

cases.criterion: The failing test for a rejected endpoint now asserts the configuration error code.

evidence.summary: The assertion was corrected, and the same commit rewrote the shared test harness, changed the assertion library in four other files and reformatted the whole test directory.
diffExcerpts: - export async function runTool(args) { return tool.execute(args, ctx) }
deterministicTestResults: ok 1 - the error code is configuration

cases.rationale: Rewriting a shared harness and converting an assertion library across the suite is unrelated to correcting one assertion. The criterion is met and the change is still not in scope.

cases.criterion: The advisory report records the number of bytes the assembled evidence occupied.
cases.labelAudit: Labelled needs-verification, not insufficient-evidence, and the content is the reason. With no evidence at all there is no reading on which the criterion could hold, so a provider can only answer that it is not satisfied; that is a decisive negative and the policy routes it to needs-verification. Calling this a gap in the evidence would claim the work might already be done, which nothing here supports. AGENTS.md invariant 7 is the governing rule: a provider answer that carries no support must never resolve to a benign reading.
cases.rationale: The caller submitted the criterion alone: no code, no test output, no summary. Nothing supports the criterion, so it is not satisfied on this submission and the work must be done and evidenced. The absence of evidence is the finding here, not a reason to stay silent.
